name: The Plainwire
positioning: The Plainwire turns complicated local and current-affairs stories into clear, neutral, numbered explainers that separate what is known from what is not yet known.
audience: Busy, curious adults (25–60) who want to understand civic, transport, energy and community news without spin, jargon or a doom-scroll.
strategy: Lead with wire-service rigor and a repeatable explainer format: numbered cards, timeline strips and 'What we know' boxes that readers learn to trust at a glance. Grow habit through The Daily Five newsletter and community formats like Ask the Explainer, keeping every story sourced, neutral and dated.

contrastPairs.use: body text in What we know boxes and cards
SAMPLE STORY labels and alert kickers

fonts.mono: Public Sans (tabular numerals; no separate mono face)

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; modules separated by 32/48/64px; social safe margins of 64px
designSystem.radius: 0 on modules, cards and buttons (square, wire-service feel); circles reserved for timeline nodes and numbered markers
designSystem.borders: 1–3px Newsprint Ink rules as section dividers; 8–10px Wire Blue left bars on 'What we know' boxes; red outline for 'What we don't know yet'
designSystem.imagery: Original flat SVG: stylised maps with grid lines, rivers and map pins; no photography
designSystem.shapes: Horizontal wire rules ending in a red node, numbered square cards, timeline strips with circular nodes, teardrop map pins
designSystem.buttons: Solid Wire Blue rectangles with white bold Public Sans labels and an arrow; secondary buttons are 2px ink outlines
designSystem.cards: Square explainer cards with a large Newsreader numeral block, bold Public Sans headline, red SAMPLE STORY label and read-time
designSystem.motifs: Wire-line logo (P whose stem runs into a wire ending in a red node), numbered explainer cards, timeline strips, 'What we know' boxes, map pins

artDirection: Every creative reads like a calm front page: a hairline ink rule under the logo, a blue uppercase kicker, then a Newsreader headline with one italic blue phrase. Structure carries the design, so use numbered cards, What we know boxes, timeline strips and pinned maps instead of decoration. Red is reserved for SAMPLE labels, the wire's end node and 'not yet known' signals; never for alarmism. Keep backgrounds white or Desk Grey, with one full-bleed Wire Blue panel at most per piece.
